73    fn load_internal<R: Read>(mut source: R, capacity: Option<usize>, options: LoadOptions) -> Result<Document> {
74        let mut buffer = capacity.map(Vec::with_capacity).unwrap_or_default();
75        source.read_to_end(&mut buffer)?;
76
77        Reader {
78            buffer: &buffer,
79            document: Document::new(),
80            encryption_state: None,
81            raw_objects: BTreeMap::new(),
82            password: options.password,
83            strict: options.strict,
84            max_decompressed_size: options.max_decompressed_size,
85            normal_offsets: Vec::new(),
86        }
87        .read(options.filter)
88    }
89

463pub struct Reader<'a> {
464    pub buffer: &'a [u8],
465    pub document: Document,
466    pub encryption_state: Option<EncryptionState>,
467    pub raw_objects: BTreeMap<ObjectId, Vec<u8>>, // Store raw bytes for encrypted objects
468    pub password: Option<String>,                 // Password for encrypted PDFs
469    pub strict: bool,                             // Reject non-conforming PDFs when true
470    /// Maximum decompressed size, in bytes, allowed for any single stream
471    /// (object streams and cross-reference streams) decoded during loading.
472    /// `None` (the default) applies no limit; set it to guard against
473    /// decompression bombs. See [`crate::third_party::lopdf::LoadOptions`].
474    pub max_decompressed_size: Option<usize>,
475    /// Sorted unique byte offsets of every `XrefEntry::Normal` entry in the
476    /// final cross-reference table. Built once when the table is complete so
477    /// object-boundary lookups can binary-search the successor offset instead
478    /// of scanning all xref entries on each call.
479    normal_offsets: Vec<usize>,
480}
481
482/// Maximum allowed embedding of literal strings.
483pub const MAX_BRACKET: usize = 100;
484
485pub const MAX_NESTING_DEPTH: usize = 100;
486
487/// PdfCraft patch: a valid stream /Length resolves in at most three lookups (the length, the object stream holding
488/// it, and that stream's own /Length); longer lookup chains overflowed the stack.
489const MAX_LOOKUP_DEPTH: usize = 16;
490
491/// Cap on reconstructed cross-reference entries, bounding memory on hostile inputs.
492const MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS: usize = 1_000_000;
493
494/// Cap on how many trailing `trailer` dictionaries are inspected for a `/Root`.
495const MAX_TRAILER_CANDIDATES: usize = 16;
496
497/// PDF metadata extracted without loading the entire document.
498/// This is useful for quickly getting basic information about large PDFs.
499#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
500pub struct PdfMetadata {
501    /// Document title from Info dictionary
502    pub title: Option<String>,
503    /// Document author from Info dictionary
504    pub author: Option<String>,
505    /// Document subject from Info dictionary
506    pub subject: Option<String>,
507    /// Document keywords from Info dictionary
508    pub keywords: Option<String>,
509    /// Application that created the document
510    pub creator: Option<String>,
511    /// Application that produced the document
512    pub producer: Option<String>,
513    /// Document creation date (PDF date format: D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm')
514    pub creation_date: Option<String>,
515    /// Document modification date (PDF date format: D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm')
516    pub modification_date: Option<String>,
517    /// Custom Info dictionary entries that are not part of the standard set above.
518    ///
519    /// Producers commonly use the Info dictionary to attach application-specific
520    /// metadata (for example, Microsoft Information Protection labels stored as
521    /// `MSIP_Label_{GUID}_{Property}` keys). Such entries used to be discarded
522    /// by the metadata-only loader; they are now preserved here as raw `Object`
523    /// values so callers can inspect or decode them as needed.
524    pub custom: HashMap<Vec<u8>, Object>,
525    /// Number of pages in the document
526    pub page_count: u32,
527    /// PDF version
528    pub version: String,
529    /// Whether the document declares encryption (an `/Encrypt` entry in the
530    /// trailer). When `true`, string and stream contents are encrypted; the
531    /// standard Info fields above are populated only if the document could be
532    /// decrypted — e.g. an empty user password, or a password supplied via a
533    /// `*_with_password` loader.
534    pub encrypted: bool,
535}
536
537struct InfoMetadata {
538    title: Option<String>,
539    author: Option<String>,
540    subject: Option<String>,
541    keywords: Option<String>,
542    creator: Option<String>,
543    producer: Option<String>,
544    creation_date: Option<String>,
545    modification_date: Option<String>,
546    custom: HashMap<Vec<u8>, Object>,
547}
548
549impl InfoMetadata {
550    fn empty() -> Self {
551        Self {
552            title: None,
553            author: None,
554            subject: None,
555            keywords: None,
556            creator: None,
557            producer: None,
558            creation_date: None,
559            modification_date: None,
560            custom: HashMap::new(),
561        }
562    }
563}
564
565/// Standard Info dictionary keys defined in PDF 1.7 §14.3.3 ("Document
566/// Information Dictionary"). Any other key is preserved on
567/// `PdfMetadata::custom` rather than dropped.
568const STANDARD_INFO_KEYS: &[&[u8]] =
569    &[b"Title", b"Author", b"Subject", b"Keywords", b"Creator", b"Producer", b"CreationDate", b"ModDate", b"Trapped"];
570
571impl Reader<'_> {
572    /// Read metadata (title and page count) without loading the entire document.
573    /// This is much faster for large PDFs when you only need basic information.
574    ///
575    /// For encrypted PDFs, use `Document::load_metadata_with_password()` instead.
576    pub fn read_metadata(mut self) -> Result<PdfMetadata> {
577        let offset = self.buffer.windows(5).position(|w| w == b"%PDF-").unwrap_or(0);
578        self.buffer = &self.buffer[offset..];
579
580        let version = parser::header(self.buffer, self.strict).ok_or(ParseError::InvalidFileHeader)?;
581
582        let (xref, trailer) = match self.resolve_xref_and_trailer() {
583            Ok(resolved) => resolved,
584            Err(err) => match self.reconstruct_xref_and_trailer() {
585                Some(reconstructed) => {
586                    warn!("cross-reference resolution failed ({err}); recovered by scanning for indirect objects");
587                    reconstructed
588                }
589                None => return Err(err),
590            },
591        };
592
593        self.set_reference_table(xref);
594        self.document.trailer = trailer.clone();
595        let encrypted = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").is_ok();
596        // For encrypted PDFs, set up decryption so the Info dictionary can be
597        // read. If the document is protected by a password we cannot supply,
598        // still report what we have (notably `encrypted`) rather than failing
599        // the whole call; callers needing the Info fields should use a
600        // `*_with_password` loader.
601        let needs_password = if encrypted {
602            match self.setup_encryption_for_metadata() {
603                Ok(()) => false,
604                // No usable password was available (empty password failed and
605                // none was supplied): report `encrypted` without the Info
606                // fields. A wrong supplied password still surfaces as an error.
607                Err(Error::Unimplemented(_)) => true,
608                Err(e) => return Err(e),
609            }
610        } else {
611            false
612        };
613
614        let info_metadata = if needs_password { InfoMetadata::empty() } else { self.extract_info_metadata()? };
615        let page_count = if needs_password { 0 } else { self.extract_page_count()? };
616
617        Ok(PdfMetadata {
618            title: info_metadata.title,
619            author: info_metadata.author,
620            subject: info_metadata.subject,
621            keywords: info_metadata.keywords,
622            creator: info_metadata.creator,
623            producer: info_metadata.producer,
624            creation_date: info_metadata.creation_date,
625            modification_date: info_metadata.modification_date,
626            custom: info_metadata.custom,
627            page_count,
628            version,
629            encrypted,
630        })
631    }
632
633    fn extract_info_metadata(&self) -> Result<InfoMetadata> {
634        let info_ref = match self.document.trailer.get(b"Info") {
635            Ok(obj) => obj.as_reference().ok(),
636            Err(_) => return Ok(InfoMetadata::empty()),
637        };
638
639        let info_id = match info_ref {
640            Some(id) => id,
641            None => return Ok(InfoMetadata::empty()),
642        };
643
644        let mut already_seen = HashSet::new();
645        let info_obj = match self.get_object(info_id, &mut already_seen) {
646            Ok(obj) => obj,
647            Err(_) => return Ok(InfoMetadata::empty()),
648        };
649
650        let info_dict = match info_obj.as_dict() {
651            Ok(dict) => dict,
652            Err(_) => return Ok(InfoMetadata::empty()),
653        };
654
655        let mut custom = HashMap::new();
656        for (key, value) in info_dict.iter() {
657            if STANDARD_INFO_KEYS.contains(&key.as_slice()) {
658                continue;
659            }
660            custom.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
661        }
662
663        Ok(InfoMetadata {
664            title: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Title"),
665            author: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Author"),
666            subject: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Subject"),
667            keywords: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Keywords"),
668            creator: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Creator"),
669            producer: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"Producer"),
670            creation_date: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"CreationDate"),
671            modification_date: Self::extract_string_field(info_dict, b"ModDate"),
672            custom,
673        })
674    }

676    fn extract_string_field(dict: &Dictionary, key: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
677        match dict.get(key) {
678            Ok(obj) => match obj {
679                Object::String(_bytes, _) => common_data_structures::decode_text_string(obj).ok(),
680                _ => None,
681            },
682            Err(_) => None,
683        }
684    }

686    fn extract_page_count(&self) -> Result<u32> {
687        let root_ref = match self.document.trailer.get(b"Root").and_then(Object::as_reference) {
688            Ok(id) => id,
689            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
690        };
691
692        let mut already_seen = HashSet::new();
693        let catalog_obj = match self.get_object(root_ref, &mut already_seen) {
694            Ok(obj) => obj,
695            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
696        };
697
698        let catalog_dict = match catalog_obj.as_dict() {
699            Ok(dict) => dict,
700            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
701        };
702
703        let pages_ref = match catalog_dict.get(b"Pages").and_then(Object::as_reference) {
704            Ok(id) => id,
705            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
706        };
707
708        self.get_pages_tree_count(pages_ref, &mut HashSet::new(), 0).or(Ok(0))
709    }
710
711    fn get_pages_tree_count(&self, pages_id: ObjectId, seen: &mut HashSet<ObjectId>, depth: usize) -> Result<u32> {
712        // `seen` catches a repeated node (a cycle); it does not bound the depth of a long,
713        // non-cyclic /Pages chain with no /Count, which recurses once per level. Cap that
714        // separately, matching this crate's existing MAX_NESTING_DEPTH budget.
715        if depth >= MAX_NESTING_DEPTH {
716            return Ok(0);
717        }
718        if seen.contains(&pages_id) {
719            return Err(Error::ReferenceCycle(pages_id));
720        }
721        seen.insert(pages_id);
722
723        let mut already_seen = HashSet::new();
724        let pages_obj = match self.get_object(pages_id, &mut already_seen) {
725            Ok(obj) => obj,
726            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
727        };
728
729        let pages_dict = match pages_obj.as_dict() {
730            Ok(dict) => dict,
731            Err(_) => return Ok(0),
732        };
733
734        match pages_dict.get_type() {
735            Ok(type_name) if type_name == b"Page" => Ok(1),
736            Ok(type_name) if type_name == b"Pages" => {
737                if let Ok(count_obj) = pages_dict.get(b"Count")
738                    && let Ok(count) = count_obj.as_i64()
739                    && count >= 0
740                {
741                    return Ok(count as u32);
742                }
743
744                let kids = match pages_dict.get(b"Kids").and_then(Object::as_array) {
745                    Ok(arr) => arr,
746                    Err(_) => return Ok(0),
747                };
748
749                let mut total = 0u32;
750                for kid in kids.iter() {
751                    if let Ok(kid_ref) = kid.as_reference()
752                        && let Ok(count) = self.get_pages_tree_count(kid_ref, seen, depth + 1)
753                    {
754                        total += count;
755                    }
756                }
757                Ok(total)
758            }
759            _ => Ok(1),
760        }
761    }
762
763    /// Read whole document.
764    pub fn read(mut self, filter_func: Option<FilterFunc>) -> Result<Document> {
765        let offset = self.buffer.windows(5).position(|w| w == b"%PDF-").unwrap_or(0);
766        self.buffer = &self.buffer[offset..];
767
768        // The document structure can be expressed in PEG as:
769        //   document <- header indirect_object* xref trailer xref_start
770        let version = parser::header(self.buffer, self.strict).ok_or(ParseError::InvalidFileHeader)?;
771
772        //The binary_mark is in line 2 after the pdf version. If at other line number, then will be declared as invalid
773        // pdf.
774        if let Some(pos) = self.buffer.iter().position(|&byte| byte == b'\n')
775            && let Some(binary_mark) = parser::binary_mark(&self.buffer[pos + 1..])
776            && binary_mark.iter().all(|&byte| byte >= 128)
777        {
778            self.document.binary_mark = binary_mark;
779        }
780
781        // Fall back to reconstruction only after all standard resolution fails.
782        let (xref, trailer) = match self.resolve_xref_and_trailer() {
783            Ok(resolved) => resolved,
784            Err(err) => match self.reconstruct_xref_and_trailer() {
785                Some(reconstructed) => {
786                    warn!("cross-reference resolution failed ({err}); recovered by scanning for indirect objects");
787                    reconstructed
788                }
789                None => return Err(err),
790            },
791        };
792
793        self.document.version = version;
794        self.document.max_id = xref.size - 1;
795        self.document.trailer = trailer;
796        self.set_reference_table(xref);
797
798        // Check if encrypted
799        let is_encrypted = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").is_ok();
800
801        if is_encrypted {
802            // For encrypted PDFs, use a special loading strategy
803            self.load_encrypted_document(filter_func)?;
804        } else {
805            // For non-encrypted PDFs, use the normal loading
806            self.load_objects_raw(filter_func)?;
807        }
808
809        // Object-stream members join `objects` only during loading, after
810        // `max_id` was derived from the xref size. Keep the ceiling at least
811        // at the highest loaded object so new ids cannot collide with live ones.
812        if let Some(&max_loaded_id) = self.document.objects.keys().next_back() {
813            self.document.max_id = self.document.max_id.max(max_loaded_id.0);
814        }
815
816        Ok(self.document)
817    }
818
819    /// Load an encrypted document: read every object's raw bytes first, then decrypt and parse
820    /// them, object streams from one shared node budget.
821    fn load_encrypted_document(&mut self, _filter_func: Option<FilterFunc>) -> Result<()> {
822        // First, extract all raw object bytes without parsing
823        let entries: Vec<_> = self.document.reference_table.entries.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v.clone())).collect();
824
825        let mut object_streams = Vec::new();
826        // PdfCraft patch: one object budget for every object stream this load parses.
827        let node_budget = NodeBudget::new(MAX_LOAD_NODES);
828
829        for (obj_num, entry) in entries {
830            match entry {
831                XrefEntry::Normal { offset, .. } => {
832                    if let Ok((obj_id, raw_bytes)) = self.extract_raw_object(offset as usize) {
833                        self.raw_objects.insert(obj_id, raw_bytes);
834                    }
835                }
836                XrefEntry::Compressed { container, index } => {
837                    // Store compressed object info for later processing
838                    object_streams.push((obj_num, container, index));
839                }
840                XrefEntry::Free | XrefEntry::UnusableFree => {
841                    // Skip free entries
842                }
843            }
844        }
845
846        self.parse_encryption_dictionary()?;
847
848        if self.authenticate_and_setup_encryption(false)?.is_none() {
849            return Ok(());
850        }
851
852        if let Some(ref state) = self.encryption_state {
853            let encrypt_ref = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").ok().and_then(|o| o.as_reference().ok());
854
855            for (obj_id, raw_bytes) in &self.raw_objects {
856                if let Some(enc_ref) = encrypt_ref
857                    && *obj_id == enc_ref
858                {
859                    continue;
860                }
861
862                if let Ok((id, mut obj)) = self.parse_raw_object(raw_bytes) {
863                    let _ = encryption::decrypt_object(state, *obj_id, &mut obj);
864                    self.document.objects.insert(id, obj);
865                }
866            }
867
868            // PdfCraft patch: object streams in object-number order, so the members a spent node
869            // budget skips are the same on every load.
870            let mut streams_to_process: BTreeMap<u32, Vec<(u32, u16)>> = BTreeMap::new();
871            for (obj_num, container_id, index) in object_streams {
872                streams_to_process.entry(container_id).or_default().push((obj_num, index));
873            }
874
875            for (container_id, objects_in_stream) in streams_to_process {
876                if let Some(container_obj) = self.document.objects.get(&(container_id, 0))
877                    && let Ok(stream) = container_obj.as_stream()
878                {
879                    // PdfCraft patch: parse only the members the table places in this stream, so
880                    // the others spend nothing from the budget.
881                    let listed: BTreeSet<u32> = objects_in_stream.iter().map(|&(obj_num, _)| obj_num).collect();
882                    let keep = |obj_num: u32| listed.contains(&obj_num);
883                    match ObjectStream::new_members_within(stream, self.max_decompressed_size, &node_budget, keep) {
884                        Ok(object_stream) => {
885                            for (obj_num, _index) in objects_in_stream {
886                                let obj_id = (obj_num, 0);
887                                if let Some(obj) = object_stream.objects.get(&obj_id) {
888                                    self.document.objects.insert(obj_id, obj.clone());
889                                }
890                            }
891                        }
892                        Err(_e) => {}
893                    }
894                }
895            }
896
897            let mut stored_state = state.clone();
898            // Record the /Encrypt dictionary's object id so that a later
899            // incremental save can restore `/Encrypt N G R` in the appended
900            // trailer. See `IncrementalDocument::save_internal`.
901            stored_state.encrypt_object_id = encrypt_ref;
902            self.document.encryption_state = Some(stored_state);
903
904            if let Some(enc_ref) = encrypt_ref {
905                self.document.objects.remove(&enc_ref);
906            }
907            self.document.trailer.remove(b"Encrypt");
908        }
909
910        Ok(())
911    }
912
913    fn parse_raw_object(&self, raw_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(ObjectId, Object)> {
914        // Parse the raw bytes as an indirect object
915        parser::indirect_object(raw_bytes, 0, None, self, &mut HashSet::new(), None)
916    }
917
918    /// Install a fully merged cross-reference table and derive its sorted
919    /// offset index. All later object-boundary lookups go through that index,
920    /// so it must be rebuilt whenever the table is replaced.
921    fn set_reference_table(&mut self, xref: Xref) {
922        let mut normal_offsets: Vec<usize> = xref
923            .entries
924            .values()
925            .filter_map(|entry| match entry {
926                XrefEntry::Normal { offset, .. } => Some(*offset as usize),
927                _ => None,
928            })
929            .collect();
930        normal_offsets.sort_unstable();
931        normal_offsets.dedup();
932        self.normal_offsets = normal_offsets;
933        self.document.reference_table = xref;
934    }
935
936    /// Load every object in the cross-reference table, expanding object streams from one node
937    /// budget shared by the whole load.
938    fn load_objects_raw(&mut self, filter_func: Option<FilterFunc>) -> Result<()> {
939        let is_encrypted = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").is_ok();
940        let zero_length_streams = Mutex::new(vec![]);
941        let object_stream_ids = Mutex::new(vec![]);
942
943        // Build a map of which container each compressed object belongs to
944        // according to the xref. This prevents stale ObjStm copies (e.g., from
945        // linearization first-page sections) from overriding the correct version.
946        let compressed_obj_containers: BTreeMap<u32, u32> = self
947            .document
948            .reference_table
949            .entries
950            .iter()
951            .filter_map(|(&id, entry)| if let XrefEntry::Compressed { container, .. } = entry { Some((id, *container)) } else { None })
952            .collect();
953        let normal_offsets = &self.normal_offsets;
954
955        let entries_filter_map = |(_, entry): (&_, &_)| -> Result<Option<(ObjectId, Object)>> {
956            if let XrefEntry::Normal { offset, .. } = *entry {
957                // read_object now handles decryption internally
958                let offset = offset as usize;
959                let next_index = normal_offsets.partition_point(|&next| next <= offset);
960                let next_object = normal_offsets.get(next_index).copied();
961                let end = self.object_end(offset, next_object);
962                let result = self.read_object_to(offset, end, None, &mut HashSet::new());
963                let (object_id, mut object) = match result {
964                    Ok(obj) => obj,
965                    Err(e) => {
966                        if is_encrypted {
967                            // Expected for some encrypted objects - but log which
968                            // ones. These failures stay non-fatal even in strict
969                            // mode because they do not indicate a malformed file.
970                            warn!("Skipping encrypted object at offset {}: {:?}", offset, e);
971                            return Ok(None);
972                        }
973                        // Lenient loading logs and skips malformed objects; strict loading fails.
974                        error!("Object load error at offset {}: {e:?}", offset);
975                        return if self.strict { Err(e) } else { Ok(None) };
976                    }
977                };
978                if let Some(filter_func) = filter_func
979                    && filter_func(object_id, &mut object).is_none()
980                {
981                    return Ok(None);
982                }
983
984                if let Ok(stream) = object.as_stream() {
985                    if stream.dict.has_type(b"ObjStm") && !is_encrypted {
986                        // PdfCraft patch: object streams are expanded after this parallel pass,
987                        // one at a time in object-number order (below).
988                        let mut object_stream_ids = object_stream_ids.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
989                        object_stream_ids.push(object_id);
990                    } else if stream.content.is_empty() {
991                        let mut zero_length_streams = zero_length_streams.lock().unwrap();
992                        zero_length_streams.push(object_id);
993                    }
994                }
995
996                Ok(Some((object_id, object)))
997            } else {
998                Ok(None)
999            }
1000        };
1001
1002        {
1003            self.document.objects = self
1004                .document
1005                .reference_table
1006                .entries
1007                .par_iter()
1008                .map(entries_filter_map)
1009                .filter_map(Result::transpose)
1010                .collect::<Result<BTreeMap<_, _>>>()?;
1011        }
1012        #[cfg(any())]
1013        {
1014            self.document.objects = self
1015                .document
1016                .reference_table
1017                .entries
1018                .iter()
1019                .map(entries_filter_map)
1020                .filter_map(Result::transpose)
1021                .collect::<Result<BTreeMap<_, _>>>()?;
1022        }
1023
1024        // PdfCraft patch: expand the object streams one at a time in object-number order, from one
1025        // node budget for the whole load, so many streams, each inside the decompression limit,
1026        // cannot together build billions of objects, and the members a spent budget skips are the
1027        // same on every load. A stream parses only the members it would add: none the table
1028        // places in another stream (stale copies), and none already loaded, as an ordinary object
1029        // or from an earlier stream, since a member never replaces an object. Those spend nothing.
1030        // Members the table doesn't list at all are still parsed (a rebuilt table lists no
1031        // compressed objects) and share the budget.
1032        let node_budget = NodeBudget::new(MAX_LOAD_NODES);
1033        let mut object_stream_ids = object_stream_ids.into_inner().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
1034        object_stream_ids.sort_unstable();
1035        object_stream_ids.dedup();
1036        for object_id in object_stream_ids {
1037            let container_id = object_id.0;
1038            let loaded = &self.document.objects;
1039            let keep =
1040                |obj_num: u32| compressed_obj_containers.get(&obj_num).is_none_or(|&c| c == container_id) && !loaded.contains_key(&(obj_num, 0));
1041            let parsed = match loaded.get(&object_id).map(Object::as_stream) {
1042                Some(Ok(stream)) => ObjectStream::new_members_within(stream, self.max_decompressed_size, &node_budget, keep),
1043                _ => continue,
1044            };
1045            match parsed {
1046                Ok(obj_stream) => {
1047                    let members: BTreeMap<_, _> = match filter_func {
1048                        Some(filter_func) => {
1049                            obj_stream.objects.into_iter().filter_map(|(object_id, mut object)| filter_func(object_id, &mut object)).collect()
1050                        }
1051                        None => obj_stream.objects,
1052                    };
1053                    // Only add entries, but never replace entries
1054                    for (id, entry) in members {
1055                        self.document.objects.entry(id).or_insert(entry);
1056                    }
1057                }
1058                // Not an encryption-related loss, so it obeys the same strict-mode policy as
1059                // any other load error; a lenient load drops the stream, as it drops any object
1060                // that fails to load.
1061                Err(e) => {
1062                    error!("Object stream load error for {object_id:?}: {e:?}");
1063                    if self.strict {
1064                        return Err(e);
1065                    }
1066                    self.document.objects.remove(&object_id);
1067                }
1068            }
1069        }
1070
1071        for object_id in zero_length_streams.into_inner().unwrap() {
1072            let _ = self.read_stream_content(object_id);
1073        }
1074
1075        Ok(())
1076    }
1077
1078    fn read_stream_content(&mut self, object_id: ObjectId) -> Result<()> {
1079        let length = self.get_stream_length(object_id)?;
1080        let stream = self.document.get_object_mut(object_id).and_then(Object::as_stream_mut)?;
1081        let start = stream.start_position.ok_or(Error::InvalidStream("missing start position".to_string()))?;
1082
1083        if length < 0 {
1084            return Err(Error::InvalidStream("negative stream length.".to_string()));
1085        }
1086
1087        let length = usize::try_from(length).map_err(|e| Error::NumericCast(e.to_string()))?;
1088        let end = start + length;
1089
1090        if end > self.buffer.len() {
1091            return Err(Error::InvalidStream("stream extends after document end.".to_string()));
1092        }
1093
1094        stream.set_content(self.buffer[start..end].to_vec());
1095        Ok(())
1096    }
1097
1098    fn get_stream_length(&self, object_id: ObjectId) -> Result<i64> {
1099        let object = self.document.get_object(object_id)?;
1100        let stream = object.as_stream()?;
1101        stream
1102            .dict
1103            .get(b"Length")
1104            .and_then(|value| self.document.dereference(value))
1105            .and_then(|(_id, obj)| match obj.as_i64() {
1106                Ok(length) => Ok(length),
1107                // ISO 32000-1 s7.3.8.2 requires /Length to be an integer, but some producers
1108                // write it as a real ("42." instead of "42"). Accept one whose value is
1109                // integral and in range rather than dropping the stream's content.
1110                Err(err) => match obj.as_f32() {
1111                    Ok(value) if value.fract() == 0.0 && value >= -(2f32.powi(63)) && value < 2f32.powi(63) => Ok(value as i64),
1112                    _ => Err(err),
1113                },
1114            })
1115            .inspect_err(|_err| {
1116                error!("stream dictionary of '{} {} R' is missing the Length entry", object_id.0, object_id.1);
1117            })
1118    }
1119
1120    /// Get object offset by object ID.
1121    fn get_offset(&self, id: ObjectId) -> Result<u32> {
1122        let entry = self.document.reference_table.get(id.0).ok_or(Error::MissingXrefEntry)?;
1123        match *entry {
1124            XrefEntry::Normal { offset, generation } if generation == id.1 => Ok(offset),
1125            _ => Err(Error::MissingXrefEntry),
1126        }
1127    }
1128
1129    /// Load a compressed object from an object stream (for lightweight metadata extraction)
1130    fn get_compressed_object(&self, id: ObjectId, already_seen: &mut HashSet<ObjectId>) -> Result<Object> {
1131        let entry = self.document.reference_table.get(id.0).ok_or(Error::MissingXrefEntry)?;
1132
1133        let container_id = match entry {
1134            XrefEntry::Compressed { container, .. } => *container,
1135            _ => return Err(Error::MissingXrefEntry),
1136        };
1137
1138        // PdfCraft patch: require an in-file container (PDF 7.5.7) and retain the caller's cycle history through
1139        // indirect stream /Length lookups; `get_object` caps the depth of that history.
1140        if !matches!(self.document.reference_table.get(container_id), Some(XrefEntry::Normal { .. })) {
1141            return Err(Error::InvalidObjectStream("Object stream container must be an ordinary in-file object".into()));
1142        }
1143        let container_id = (container_id, 0);
1144        let container_obj = self.get_object(container_id, already_seen)?;
1145        let container_stream = container_obj.as_stream()?;
1146        // PdfCraft patch: a lookup parses only the member it wants, from one object's budget
1147        // rather than a load's, so the members before it can't spend that budget first.
1148        let budget = NodeBudget::new(parser::MAX_OBJECT_NODES);
1149        let mut object_stream = ObjectStream::new_members_within(container_stream, self.max_decompressed_size, &budget, |obj_num| obj_num == id.0)?;
1150        object_stream.objects.remove(&id).ok_or(Error::MissingXrefEntry)
1151    }
1152
1153    pub fn get_object(&self, id: ObjectId, already_seen: &mut HashSet<ObjectId>) -> Result<Object> {
1154        // PdfCraft patch: each top-level lookup starts with an empty set and every nested lookup adds one object, so
1155        // the set's size is the depth of the lookup chain.
1156        if already_seen.len() >= MAX_LOOKUP_DEPTH {
1157            warn!("lookup chain deeper than {MAX_LOOKUP_DEPTH} at object {} {}", id.0, id.1);
1158            return Err(Error::ReferenceLimit);
1159        }
1160        if already_seen.contains(&id) {
1161            warn!("reference cycle detected resolving object {} {}", id.0, id.1);
1162            return Err(Error::ReferenceCycle(id));
1163        }
1164        already_seen.insert(id);
1165
1166        if let Some(entry) = self.document.reference_table.get(id.0)
1167            && matches!(entry, XrefEntry::Compressed { .. })
1168        {
1169            return self.get_compressed_object(id, already_seen);
1170        }
1171
1172        let offset = self.get_offset(id)?;
1173        let (_, mut obj) = self.read_object(offset as usize, Some(id), already_seen)?;
1174
1175        if let Some(ref state) = self.encryption_state {
1176            let encrypt_ref = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").ok().and_then(|o| o.as_reference().ok());
1177            if let Some(enc_ref) = encrypt_ref
1178                && id != enc_ref
1179            {
1180                encryption::decrypt_object(state, id, &mut obj).map_err(Error::Decryption)?;
1181            }
1182        }
1183
1184        Ok(obj)
1185    }
1186
1187    fn parse_encryption_dictionary(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
1188        if let Ok(encrypt_ref) = self.document.trailer.get(b"Encrypt").and_then(|o| o.as_reference()) {
1189            if self.raw_objects.is_empty() {
1190                let offset = self.get_offset(encrypt_ref)?;
1191                let (_, encrypt_obj) = self.read_object(offset as usize, Some(encrypt_ref), &mut HashSet::new())?;
1192                self.document.objects.insert(encrypt_ref, encrypt_obj);
1193            } else if let Some(raw_bytes) = self.raw_objects.get(&encrypt_ref)
1194                && let Ok((_, obj)) = self.parse_raw_object(raw_bytes)
1195            {
1196                self.document.objects.insert(encrypt_ref, obj);
1197            }
1198        }
1199        Ok(())
1200    }
1201
1202    fn authenticate_and_setup_encryption(&mut self, require_password: bool) -> Result<Option<String>> {
1203        let password_to_use: Option<String> = if self.document.authenticate_password("").is_ok() {
1204            Some(String::new())
1205        } else if let Some(ref pwd) = self.password {
1206            if self.document.authenticate_password(pwd).is_ok() {
1207                Some(pwd.clone())
1208            } else if require_password {
1209                return Err(Error::InvalidPassword);
1210            } else {
1211                warn!("Invalid password provided for encrypted PDF");
1212                return Err(Error::InvalidPassword);
1213            }
1214        } else if require_password {
1215            return Err(Error::Unimplemented("PDF is encrypted and requires a password. Use Document::load_metadata_with_password() instead."));
1216        } else {
1217            warn!("PDF is encrypted and requires a password");
1218            return Ok(None);
1219        };
1220
1221        if let Some(ref password) = password_to_use {
1222            let state = EncryptionState::decode(&self.document, password)?;
1223            self.encryption_state = Some(state);
1224        }
1225
1226        Ok(password_to_use)
1227    }
1228
1229    fn setup_encryption_for_metadata(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
1230        self.parse_encryption_dictionary()?;
1231        self.authenticate_and_setup_encryption(true)?;
1232        Ok(())
1233    }
1234
1235    fn extract_raw_object(&mut self, offset: usize) -> Result<(ObjectId, Vec<u8>)> {
1236        if offset > self.buffer.len() {
1237            return Err(Error::InvalidOffset(offset));
1238        }
1239
1240        // Find object header (e.g., "19 0 obj")
1241        let slice = &self.buffer[offset..];
1242
1243        // Parse object ID
1244        let mut pos = 0;
1245        while pos < slice.len() && slice[pos].is_ascii_whitespace() {
1246            pos += 1;
1247        }
1248
1249        // Get object number
1250        let num_start = pos;
1251        while pos < slice.len() && slice[pos].is_ascii_digit() {
1252            pos += 1;
1253        }
1254        let obj_num: u32 =
1255            std::str::from_utf8(&slice[num_start..pos]).ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).ok_or(Error::Parse(ParseError::InvalidXref))?;
1256
1257        // Skip whitespace
1258        while pos < slice.len() && slice[pos].is_ascii_whitespace() {
1259            pos += 1;
1260        }
1261
1262        // Get generation number
1263        let gen_start = pos;
1264        while pos < slice.len() && slice[pos].is_ascii_digit() {
1265            pos += 1;
1266        }
1267        let obj_gen: u16 =
1268            std::str::from_utf8(&slice[gen_start..pos]).ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).ok_or(Error::Parse(ParseError::InvalidXref))?;
1269
1270        // Skip to "obj"
1271        while pos < slice.len() && slice[pos].is_ascii_whitespace() {
1272            pos += 1;
1273        }
1274        if pos + 3 > slice.len() || &slice[pos..pos + 3] != b"obj" {
1275            return Err(Error::Parse(ParseError::InvalidXref));
1276        }
1277        pos += 3;
1278
1279        // Find "endobj"
1280        let endobj_pattern = b"endobj";
1281        let mut end_pos = pos;
1282        while end_pos + endobj_pattern.len() <= slice.len() {
1283            if &slice[end_pos..end_pos + endobj_pattern.len()] == endobj_pattern {
1284                end_pos += endobj_pattern.len();
1285                break;
1286            }
1287            end_pos += 1;
1288        }
1289
1290        if end_pos > slice.len() {
1291            return Err(Error::Parse(ParseError::InvalidXref));
1292        }
1293
1294        // Extract raw object bytes (including header and trailer)
1295        let raw_bytes = slice[0..end_pos].to_vec();
1296
1297        Ok(((obj_num, obj_gen), raw_bytes))
1298    }
1299
1300    fn read_object(&self, offset: usize, expected_id: Option<ObjectId>, already_seen: &mut HashSet<ObjectId>) -> Result<(ObjectId, Object)> {
1301        let next_index = self.normal_offsets.partition_point(|&next| next <= offset);
1302        let end = self.object_end(offset, self.normal_offsets.get(next_index).copied());
1303        self.read_object_to(offset, end, expected_id, already_seen)
1304    }
1305
1306    fn object_end(&self, offset: usize, next_object: Option<usize>) -> usize {
1307        let xref_start = (self.document.xref_start > offset).then_some(self.document.xref_start);
1308        next_object.into_iter().chain(xref_start).min().unwrap_or(self.buffer.len()).min(self.buffer.len())
1309    }
1310
1311    fn read_object_to(
1312        &self,
1313        offset: usize,
1314        end: usize,
1315        expected_id: Option<ObjectId>,
1316        already_seen: &mut HashSet<ObjectId>,
1317    ) -> Result<(ObjectId, Object)> {
1318        if offset > end || end > self.buffer.len() {
1319            return Err(Error::InvalidOffset(offset));
1320        }
1321
1322        // Objects are parsed against the full buffer so a wrong *neighbor*
1323        // xref offset cannot truncate a well-formed object; `end` only limits
1324        // how far malformed-stream length recovery may scan.
1325        parser::indirect_object(self.buffer, offset, expected_id, self, already_seen, Some(end))
1326    }
1327
1328    /// Parse the cross-reference section recorded at `offset`, first correcting
1329    /// the offset if it is slightly miswritten (lenient mode only).
1330    fn xref_and_trailer_at(&self, offset: usize) -> Result<(Xref, Dictionary)> {
1331        let offset = self.correct_xref_offset(offset);
1332        parser::xref_and_trailer(&self.buffer[offset..], self)
1333    }
1334
1335    /// Resolve the cross-reference table/stream and trailer, including the
1336    /// `/Prev` chain, and record the resolved start offset on the document.
1337    fn resolve_xref_and_trailer(&mut self) -> Result<(Xref, Dictionary)> {
1338        let xref_start = Self::get_xref_start(self.buffer)?;
1339        if xref_start > self.buffer.len() {
1340            return Err(Error::Xref(XrefError::Start));
1341        }
1342        let xref_start = self.correct_xref_offset(xref_start);
1343        self.document.xref_start = xref_start;
1344
1345        let (mut xref, mut trailer) = self.xref_and_trailer_at(xref_start)?;
1346
1347        // Read previous Xrefs of linearized or incremental updated document.
1348        let mut already_seen = HashSet::new();
1349        let mut prev_xref_start = trailer.remove(b"Prev");
1350        while let Some(prev) = prev_xref_start.and_then(|offset| offset.as_i64().ok()) {
1351            if already_seen.contains(&prev) {
1352                break;
1353            }
1354            already_seen.insert(prev);
1355            if prev < 0 || prev as usize > self.buffer.len() {
1356                return Err(Error::Xref(XrefError::PrevStart));
1357            }
1358
1359            let (prev_xref, prev_trailer) = self.xref_and_trailer_at(prev as usize)?;
1360            xref.merge(prev_xref);
1361
1362            // Read xref stream in hybrid-reference file
1363            let prev_xref_stream_start = trailer.remove(b"XRefStm");
1364            if let Some(prev) = prev_xref_stream_start.and_then(|offset| offset.as_i64().ok()) {
1365                if prev < 0 || prev as usize > self.buffer.len() {
1366                    return Err(Error::Xref(XrefError::StreamStart));
1367                }
1368
1369                let (prev_xref, _) = self.xref_and_trailer_at(prev as usize)?;
1370                xref.merge(prev_xref);
1371            }
1372
1373            prev_xref_start = prev_trailer.get(b"Prev").cloned().ok();
1374        }
1375        let xref_entry_count = xref.max_id().checked_add(1).ok_or(ParseError::InvalidXref)?;
1376        if xref.size != xref_entry_count {
1377            warn!("Size entry of trailer dictionary is {}, correct value is {}.", xref.size, xref_entry_count);
1378            xref.size = xref_entry_count;
1379        }
1380
1381        Ok((xref, trailer))
1382    }
1383
1384    /// Last-resort recovery: rebuild the cross-reference table by scanning the
1385    /// raw bytes for indirect-object headers and locating a trailer with a
1386    /// usable `/Root`. Returns `None` (caller keeps the original error) when
1387    /// strict mode forbids recovery or nothing usable was found.
1388    fn reconstruct_xref_and_trailer(&mut self) -> Option<(Xref, Dictionary)> {
1389        if self.strict {
1390            return None;
1391        }
1392        u32::try_from(self.buffer.len()).ok()?;
1393
1394        let markers = Self::scan_object_markers(self.buffer);
1395        if markers.is_empty() {
1396            return None;
1397        }
1398
1399        let mut xref = Xref::new(markers.len() as u32, XrefType::CrossReferenceTable);
1400        for (offset, (number, generation)) in markers {
1401            // Incremental updates append, so later revisions win.
1402            xref.insert(number, XrefEntry::Normal { offset, generation });
1403        }
1404        // Normalize like `resolve_xref_and_trailer`: size spans object numbers
1405        // up to the highest, not physical copies across incremental updates.
1406        xref.size = xref.max_id().saturating_add(1);
1407
1408        let (_trailer_pos, trailer) = self.find_latest_trailer(&xref)?;
1409        // deliberate: no on-disk table exists to point at. Zero marks the
1410        // offset "unknown" so `Document::new_from_prev` omits `/Prev` instead
1411        // of recording end-of-file; `object_end` clamps to the buffer either way.
1412        self.document.xref_start = 0;
1413
1414        warn!("reconstructed cross-reference table with {} objects by scanning for indirect objects", xref.entries.len());
1415        Some((xref, trailer))
1416    }
1417
1418    /// Collect `(offset, id)` of every indirect-object header in one pass.
1419    /// Only headers starting a line (optional leading blanks allowed) count,
1420    /// stream payloads are skipped wholesale, and object numbers beyond
1421    /// [`MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS`] are rejected so a forged header can
1422    /// neither shadow a genuine entry nor poison the reconstructed size.
1423    fn scan_object_markers(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<(u32, ObjectId)> {
1424        const STREAM_KEYWORD: &[u8] = b"stream";
1425        const END_STREAM_KEYWORD: &[u8] = b"endstream";
1426
1427        let mut markers = Vec::new();
1428        let mut oversized_number_warned = false;
1429        let mut at_line_start = true;
1430        let mut pos = 0;
1431        while pos < buffer.len() {
1432            // Skip raw stream data: an uncompressed payload may embed
1433            // convincing `N G obj` lines whose later offsets would otherwise
1434            // override the genuine entries for those object numbers.
1435            if buffer[pos..].starts_with(STREAM_KEYWORD)
1436                && !buffer[..pos].ends_with(b"end")
1437                && matches!(buffer.get(pos + STREAM_KEYWORD.len()), Some(b'\r' | b'\n'))
1438            {
1439                let after_keyword = pos + STREAM_KEYWORD.len();
1440                if let Some(relative) = buffer[after_keyword..].windows(END_STREAM_KEYWORD.len()).position(|window| window == END_STREAM_KEYWORD) {
1441                    pos = after_keyword + relative + END_STREAM_KEYWORD.len();
1442                    at_line_start = false;
1443                    continue;
1444                }
1445                // Damaged stream without terminator: fall back to the
1446                // dictionary's /Length hint so the payload cannot hide
1447                // line-start pseudo headers, while objects written after it
1448                // stay reachable.
1449                if let Some(resume) = Self::payload_end_by_length(buffer, pos) {
1450                    pos = resume;
1451                    at_line_start = false;
1452                    continue;
1453                }
1454                // Unusable /Length too: nothing bounds the payload, so keep
1455                // scanning byte by byte rather than dropping what follows.
1456            }
1457            // Anchor at line starts so pseudo headers buried after another
1458            // token (string literal, comment) are never mistaken for markers.
1459            if at_line_start
1460                && buffer[pos].is_ascii_digit()
1461                && let Some(id) = Self::parse_object_header(&buffer[pos..])
1462            {
1463                // A huge bogus number would inflate `size` (and thus
1464                // `max_id`) via `Xref::insert`; genuine numbering stays
1465                // within the same cap as the marker count.
1466                if id.0 > MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS as u32 {
1467                    if !oversized_number_warned {
1468                        warn!("ignoring object headers numbered above {MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS}");
1469                        oversized_number_warned = true;
1470                    }
1471                } else {
1472                    if markers.len() == MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS {
1473                        warn!("object marker scan stopped at the {MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_OBJECTS}-marker cap; reconstruction may be incomplete");
1474                        break;
1475                    }
1476                    markers.push((pos as u32, id));
1477                }
1478            }
1479            match buffer[pos] {
1480                b'\r' | b'\n' => at_line_start = true,
1481                b' ' | b'\t' => {}
1482                _ => at_line_start = false,
1483            }
1484            pos += 1;
1485        }
1486        markers
1487    }
1488
1489    /// Resume offset past a stream payload according to a *direct* `/Length`
1490    /// integer in the dictionary preceding the `stream` keyword at
1491    /// `stream_pos`. The search is scoped to the current object (after the
1492    /// nearest preceding `obj` keyword) so a missing `/Length` cannot latch
1493    /// onto a previous object's value. Returns `None` when the hint is
1494    /// absent, indirect, or points outside the buffer — damaged files tend
1495    /// to carry wrong `/Length` values, so it must stay a hint, never a hard
1496    /// boundary.
1497    fn payload_end_by_length(buffer: &[u8], stream_pos: usize) -> Option<usize> {
1498        const LENGTH_KEY: &[u8] = b"/Length";
1499        const OBJ_KEYWORD: &[u8] = b"obj";
1500        const STREAM_KEYWORD_LEN: usize = b"stream".len();
1501
1502        let head = &buffer[..stream_pos];
1503        let obj_pos = head.windows(OBJ_KEYWORD.len()).rposition(|window| window == OBJ_KEYWORD)?;
1504        let dict_region = &buffer[obj_pos + OBJ_KEYWORD.len()..stream_pos];
1505        // Nearest `/Length` in this object's dictionary; parsing it validates
1506        // that the match really is a key with an integer value.
1507        let key_pos = dict_region.windows(LENGTH_KEY.len()).rposition(|window| window == LENGTH_KEY)?;
1508        let rest = &dict_region[key_pos + LENGTH_KEY.len()..];
1509        let digits_start = rest.iter().position(u8::is_ascii_digit)?;
1510        let digits_len = rest[digits_start..].iter().take_while(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()).count();
1511        if digits_len > 10 {
1512            return None;
1513        }
1514        // An indirect reference (`/Length 5 0 R`) continues with another
1515        // number token; a direct integer ends at a name, `>>`, or the keyword.
1516        match rest[digits_start + digits_len..].iter().copied().find(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace()) {
1517            Some(b'/') | Some(b'>') => {}
1518            _ => return None,
1519        }
1520        let length: usize = std::str::from_utf8(&rest[digits_start..digits_start + digits_len]).ok()?.parse().ok()?;
1521        // Spec: the EOL after the `stream` keyword counts as CRLF or LF.
1522        let eol_len = match (buffer.get(stream_pos + STREAM_KEYWORD_LEN), buffer.get(stream_pos + STREAM_KEYWORD_LEN + 1)) {
1523            (Some(b'\r'), Some(b'\n')) => 2,
1524            _ => 1,
1525        };
1526        let end = (stream_pos + STREAM_KEYWORD_LEN + eol_len).checked_add(length)?;
1527        (buffer.len() >= end).then_some(end)
1528    }
1529
1530    /// Parse an `N G obj` header; the byte after `obj` must end the token.
1531    fn parse_object_header(input: &[u8]) -> Option<ObjectId> {
1532        // deliberate: caps at u32/u16 width bound work on pathological padding.
1533        fn digits(input: &[u8], cap: usize) -> Option<(&[u8], &[u8])> {
1534            let n = input.iter().take_while(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()).count();
1535            (0 < n && n <= cap).then(|| input.split_at(n))
1536        }
1537        fn spaces(input: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]> {
1538            let n = input.iter().take_while(|&&b| matches!(b, b' ' | b'\t' | b'\r' | b'\n')).count();
1539            (n > 0).then(|| &input[n..])
1540        }
1541
1542        let (number, rest) = digits(input, 10)?;
1543        let number: u32 = std::str::from_utf8(number).ok()?.parse().ok()?;
1544        let rest = spaces(rest)?;
1545        let (generation, rest) = digits(rest, 5)?;
1546        let generation: u16 = std::str::from_utf8(generation).ok()?.parse().ok()?;
1547        let rest = spaces(rest)?;
1548        let tail = rest.strip_prefix(b"obj")?;
1549        match tail.first() {
1550            None => {}
1551            Some(&byte) if !byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() => {}
1552            _ => return None,
1553        }
1554        Some((number, generation))
1555    }
1556
1557    /// Newest backwards-scanned `trailer` whose `/Root` references a scanned object, one whose
1558    /// `/Root` is the catalog first.
1559    fn find_latest_trailer(&self, xref: &Xref) -> Option<(usize, Dictionary)> {
1560        // PdfCraft patch: (#2365) an in-file /Root must also match its generation, as
1561        // `get_offset` requires when the root is loaded.
1562        let usable = |dict: &Dictionary| {
1563            dict.get(b"Root").and_then(Object::as_reference).is_ok_and(|root| match xref.entries.get(&root.0) {
1564                Some(XrefEntry::Normal { generation, .. }) => *generation == root.1,
1565                entry => entry.is_some(),
1566            })
1567        };
1568        // PdfCraft patch: (#2365) a candidate whose /Root is the catalog (`/Type /Catalog` or
1569        // `/Pages`) beats one whose /Root is another dictionary, such as /Info, wherever it is;
1570        // the other kind is still taken when nothing better is there (an FDF's /Root).
1571        let is_catalog = |dict: &Dictionary| {
1572            let Ok(root) = dict.get(b"Root").and_then(Object::as_reference) else {
1573                return false;
1574            };
1575            let Some(XrefEntry::Normal { offset, generation }) = xref.entries.get(&root.0) else {
1576                return false;
1577            };
1578            if *generation != root.1 {
1579                return false;
1580            }
1581            parser::indirect_object(self.buffer, *offset as usize, None, self, &mut HashSet::new(), None)
1582                .ok()
1583                .and_then(|(_, object)| object.as_dict().map(|d| d.has_type(b"Catalog") || d.has(b"Pages")).ok())
1584                .unwrap_or(false)
1585        };
1586        let mut latest: Option<(bool, usize, Dictionary)> = None;
1587        let mut bound = self.buffer.len();
1588        for _ in 0..MAX_TRAILER_CANDIDATES {
1589            let Some(pos) = Reader::search_substring(&self.buffer[..bound], b"trailer", 0) else {
1590                break;
1591            };
1592            bound = pos;
1593
1594            let after_keyword = &self.buffer[pos + b"trailer".len()..];
1595            let Some(dict_start) = after_keyword.iter().position(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace()) else {
1596                continue;
1597            };
1598            let Ok((_, dict)) = parser::dictionary(&after_keyword[dict_start..]) else {
1599                continue;
1600            };
1601            if usable(&dict) {
1602                let catalog = is_catalog(&dict);
1603                if latest.is_none() || catalog {
1604                    latest = Some((catalog, pos, dict));
1605                }
1606                if catalog {
1607                    break;
1608                }
1609            }
1610        }
1611        // PdfCraft patch: (#2365) a file whose only trailer is a cross-reference stream has
1612        // no `trailer` keyword, so the scan above found nothing and the rebuild failed; its
1613        // /Info and /ID were then lost. Such a stream's dictionary is the trailer, and the
1614        // latest one in the file wins, as a later `trailer` keyword would.
1615        const HEADER_WINDOW: usize = 32;
1616        const DICT_WINDOW: usize = 4096;
1617        for entry in xref.entries.values() {
1618            let XrefEntry::Normal { offset, .. } = entry else {
1619                continue;
1620            };
1621            let offset = *offset as usize;
1622            if latest.as_ref().is_some_and(|(catalog, pos, _)| *catalog && *pos >= offset) {
1623                continue;
1624            }
1625            let Some(head) = self.buffer.get(offset..) else {
1626                continue;
1627            };
1628            let Some(dict_start) = head[..cmp::min(head.len(), HEADER_WINDOW)].windows(2).position(|window| window == b"<<") else {
1629                continue;
1630            };
1631            let dict_bytes = &head[dict_start..cmp::min(head.len(), dict_start + DICT_WINDOW)];
1632            if !dict_bytes.windows(5).any(|window| window == b"/XRef") {
1633                continue;
1634            }
1635            let Ok((_, dict)) = parser::dictionary(&head[dict_start..]) else {
1636                continue;
1637            };
1638            if dict.has_type(b"XRef") && usable(&dict) {
1639                let rank = (is_catalog(&dict), offset);
1640                if latest.as_ref().is_none_or(|(catalog, pos, _)| rank > (*catalog, *pos)) {
1641                    latest = Some((rank.0, offset, dict));
1642                }
1643            }
1644        }
1645        latest.map(|(_, pos, dict)| (pos, dict))
1646    }
1647
1648    /// Some generators write `startxref` (or trailer `Prev`) values that are
1649    /// slightly off — most commonly the offset of the line *after* the `xref`
1650    /// keyword instead of the keyword itself. Such files are otherwise intact,
1651    /// and common readers (Acrobat, poppler, mupdf, pdf.js) recover from them.
1652    /// In lenient mode, if `offset` does not point at a cross-reference table
1653    /// or an indirect object (cross-reference stream), scan a small window
1654    /// around it for the `xref` keyword and use the nearest match instead.
1655    fn correct_xref_offset(&self, offset: usize) -> usize {
1656        const RECOVERY_WINDOW: usize = 64;
1657
1658        if self.strict || offset >= self.buffer.len() {
1659            return offset;
1660        }
1661        let rest = &self.buffer[offset..];
1662        if rest.starts_with(b"xref") || Self::starts_indirect_object(rest) {
1663            return offset;
1664        }
1665
1666        let window_start = offset.saturating_sub(RECOVERY_WINDOW);
1667        let window_end = cmp::min(self.buffer.len(), offset + RECOVERY_WINDOW);
1668        let mut corrected: Option<usize> = None;
1669        for pos in window_start..window_end.saturating_sub(4) {
1670            if !self.buffer[pos..].starts_with(b"xref") {
1671                continue;
1672            }
1673            // `startxref` contains `xref`; never match inside it.
1674            if pos >= 5 && &self.buffer[pos - 5..pos] == b"start" {
1675                continue;
1676            }
1677            if corrected.is_none_or(|best: usize| pos.abs_diff(offset) < best.abs_diff(offset)) {
1678                corrected = Some(pos);
1679            }
1680        }
1681        match corrected {
1682            Some(pos) => {
1683                warn!("Cross-reference offset {} does not point at an xref section; using nearby offset {} instead.", offset, pos);
1684                pos
1685            }
1686            None => offset,
1687        }
1688    }
1689
1690    /// Whether `input` begins with an indirect-object header (`N G obj`), the
1691    /// form a cross-reference stream starts with.
1692    fn starts_indirect_object(input: &[u8]) -> bool {
1693        Self::parse_object_header(input).is_some()
1694    }
1695
1696    fn get_xref_start(buffer: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {
1697        let seek_pos = buffer.len() - cmp::min(buffer.len(), 512);
1698        Self::search_substring(buffer, b"%%EOF", seek_pos)
1699            .filter(|&eof_pos| eof_pos > 25)
1700            .and_then(|eof_pos| Self::search_substring(&buffer[..eof_pos], b"startxref", eof_pos - 25))
1701            .ok_or(Error::Xref(XrefError::Start))
1702            .and_then(|xref_pos| {
1703                if xref_pos <= buffer.len() {
1704                    match parser::xref_start(&buffer[xref_pos..]) {
1705                        Some(startxref) => Ok(startxref as usize),
1706                        None => Err(Error::Xref(XrefError::Start)),
1707                    }
1708                } else {
1709                    Err(Error::Xref(XrefError::Start))
1710                }
1711            })
1712    }
1713
1714    fn search_substring(buffer: &[u8], pattern: &[u8], start_pos: usize) -> Option<usize> {
1715        buffer.get(start_pos..)?.windows(pattern.len()).rposition(|window| window == pattern).map(|pos| start_pos + pos)
1716    }
1717}

1868#[cfg(any())]
1869#[cfg(any())]
1870fn get_xref_start_ignores_startxref_past_eof() {
1871    // Simulate a PDF with two revisions where the second has a corrupted %%EOF.
1872    // The valid %%EOF is at a known position; a second startxref appears after it
1873    // but belongs to the corrupted revision. get_xref_start must pick the
1874    // startxref *before* the valid %%EOF.
1875    let mut buf = Vec::new();
1876    // Padding so the buffer is large enough
1877    buf.extend_from_slice(&[b' '; 200]);
1878    // First (correct) startxref + xref offset + valid %%EOF
1879    let xref_offset = 100usize;
1880    let startxref_block = format!("startxref\n{}\n%%EOF\n", xref_offset);
1881    let _startxref_pos = buf.len();
1882    buf.extend_from_slice(startxref_block.as_bytes());
1883    // Second (corrupted) revision: another startxref pointing elsewhere, with %%EO\0
1884    let bad_block = "startxref\n999\n%%EO\x00\n".to_string();
1885    buf.extend_from_slice(bad_block.as_bytes());
1886
1887    let result = Reader::get_xref_start(&buf).unwrap();
1888    // Should find the xref_offset from the first startxref (before valid %%EOF)
1889    assert_eq!(result, xref_offset);
1890    // Verify it did NOT pick up 999 from the corrupted revision
1891    assert_ne!(result, 999);
1892}

1894#[cfg(any())]
1895#[cfg(any())]
1896fn recovers_from_miswritten_startxref_offset() {
1897    // Some generators write the offset of the line *after* the `xref` keyword
1898    // into `startxref` instead of the offset of the keyword itself. Lenient
1899    // loading must recover; strict loading must still reject the file.
1900    let header = "%PDF-1.5\n";
1901    let obj1 = "1 0 obj<</Type/Catalog/Pages 2 0 R>>endobj\n";
1902    let obj2 = "2 0 obj<</Type/Pages/Kids[]/Count 0>>endobj\n";
1903    let o1 = header.len();
1904    let o2 = o1 + obj1.len();
1905    let body = format!("{header}{obj1}{obj2}");
1906    let xref_pos = body.len();
1907    let doc = format!(
1908        "{body}xref
19090 3
19100000000000 65535 f 
1911{o1:010} 00000 n 
1912{o2:010} 00000 n 
1913trailer
1914<</Root 1 0 R/Size 3>>
1915startxref
1916{}
1917%%EOF",
1918        xref_pos + 4 // past the `xref` keyword, onto the line after it
1919    );
1920
1921    let loaded = Document::load_mem(doc.as_bytes()).unwrap();
1922    assert!(loaded.trailer.get(b"Root").is_ok());
1923    assert_eq!(loaded.xref_start, xref_pos);
1924
1925    let strict = Document::load_mem_with_options(doc.as_bytes(), LoadOptions { strict: true, ..Default::default() });
1926    assert!(strict.is_err());
1927}

1930#[cfg(any())]
1931fn stream_length_written_as_real() {
1932    // ISO 32000-1 s7.3.8.2 requires /Length to be an integer, but some generators
1933    // emit "/Length 42." instead of "/Length 42". Such a stream must still resolve
1934    // to its content rather than silently loading as empty.
1935    let obj4 = "4 0 obj\n<< /Length 42. >>\nstream\nBT /F1 12 Tf 20 100 Td (Hello World) Tj ET\nendstream\nendobj\n";
1936    let header = "%PDF-1.7\n";
1937    let obj1 = "1 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>\nendobj\n";
1938    let obj2 = "2 0 obj\n<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>\nendobj\n";
1939    let obj3 = "3 0 obj\n<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 200 200] /Contents 4 0 R >>\nendobj\n";
1940    let o1 = header.len();
1941    let o2 = o1 + obj1.len();
1942    let o3 = o2 + obj2.len();
1943    let o4 = o3 + obj3.len();
1944    let body = format!("{header}{obj1}{obj2}{obj3}{obj4}");
1945    let xref_pos = body.len();
1946    let doc = format!(
1947        "{body}xref
19480 5
19490000000000 65535 f 
1950{o1:010} 00000 n 
1951{o2:010} 00000 n 
1952{o3:010} 00000 n 
1953{o4:010} 00000 n 
1954trailer
1955<< /Size 5 /Root 1 0 R >>
1956startxref
1957{xref_pos}
1958%%EOF
1959"
1960    );
1961
1962    let loaded = Document::load_mem(doc.as_bytes()).unwrap();
1963    let stream = loaded.get_object((4, 0)).unwrap().as_stream().unwrap();
1964    assert_eq!(stream.content, b"BT /F1 12 Tf 20 100 Td (Hello World) Tj ET");
1965}

1968#[cfg(any())]
1969fn object_marker_parsing_accepts_only_real_headers() {
1970    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"12 0 obj<<"), Some((12, 0)));
1971    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"007 0 obj\n"), Some((7, 0)));
1972    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"5 2 obj>>"), Some((5, 2)));
1973    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"12\t3\r\nobj["), Some((12, 3)));
1974    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"2 0 objects"), None);
1975    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"99 88 objx"), None);
1976    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"12345678901 0 obj"), None);
1977    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"1 70000 obj"), None);
1978    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"1 0obj"), None);
1979    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"1  obj"), None);
1980    assert_eq!(Reader::parse_object_header(b"x 0 obj"), None);
1981}
